fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the front of the residence without obstruction.
• Trim any shrubs or trees near the detached structure so responders can move around it and see it clearly on approach.
• Mark or clearly identify any rear access points so responders are not delayed searching for a secondary way around the property.
• Keep the walkway between the front driveway and the main entrance free of obstacles so responders can move quickly on foot.
• Trim vegetation along the sides of the driveway to maintain clear sightlines and enough width for emergency vehicles to pass through.
• Designate a flat, open area within the front lawn or parking area where emergency vehicles can stage without blocking the driveway.
• If a gate or fence restricts rear access, keep it unlocked or install a Knox-style lockbox so responders can reach the back of the property without delay.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or relocate wood piles away from the exterior walls of the structure to reduce flammable material directly against the building.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between tree canopies and the roofline.
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the structure's exterior walls.
• Clear ground vegetation growing directly against the foundation and base of exterior walls.
• Separate shrub clusters near the structure so individual shrubs are not touching or overlapping each other.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure free of dry or dead ground vegetation.
• Move wood piles to a hard surface or open area with clear separation from the structure and any nearby shrubs or trees.
• Thin tree branches that hang directly over the structure or wood storage areas.
